chunks: And by this chain, from Abdullah ibn Jundab who said:

'Ubbad ibn Maymoun was asked, and I was present, about a man who made a vow upon himself for fasting, and he wanted to travel to Mecca. So Abdullah ibn Jundab said: 'I heard from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who made a vow upon himself for fasting, and his intention presented itself regarding the visitation of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should go out and not fast during the journey. So when he returns, he fulfills that (fasts the days he missed).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who has vowed to fast but needs to travel for ziyarah?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of ease (taysir) in Islamic jurisprudence, allowing a traveler to suspend a personal vow of fasting to perform the highly meritorious ziyarah of the Imam. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that fulfilling a specific religious duty (ziyarah) can take precedence over a self-imposed vow, provided the obligation is fulfilled upon return. This ruling underscores the balance between individual piety and communal or devotional practices in Shia fiqh.
